subject: We might change a default parameter...

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: We might change a default parameter...
parts:
Dear all,

we have experienced some issues with the parameter 'h', with default
value

control.inla=list(h=0.01)

and we consider to lower the default value to 0.005 or maybe even to
0.001.

This parameter is the step-size for the hyperparameters when computing
numerical gradients, and sqrt(h) is used for the step-size when
computing the Hessian.

Our concern is that when we're moving to more multi-threaded cases (more
cores, more parallel), then we have recently seen cases where 0.005 is
way better than 0.01, in terms of robustness and the ease of locating
the mode for the hyperparameters.

We would like to know if a change to one of the possible new values
creates issues in your models, either to the better or to the worse.
If would help us very much, if you could try the two new values in your
typical applications, and let us know to either this email, or to
he...@r-inla.org if you are experiencing negative or positive issues wrt
this change. If all is the same as before (I guess this is for almost
all cases!), we do not need any feedback.


Thanks

Håvard & Finn




--
Håvard Rue
hr...@r-inla.org

messages.author: a259015b36a46546
messages.subject: Re: We might change a default parameter...
parts:
Hello Håvard & Finn,

When I specify the with default value control.inla=list(h=0.001) or  control.inla=list(h=0.005)  I get a warning message which asks to set the eigenvalue to XXXX (a figure). When I use that figure or value I also get another  warning message specifying a new value. 

Running the model without specifying the Hessian value also gives a warning message. The formula and model I used are below

formula1 <- U5MR ~ SEC + FEMP + GDP + OPH + HEXP + WATER + DEF + SANI + PM2.5 +
  f(OBJECTID, model = "bym2", graph = Global.adj.path, scale.model = TRUE, hyper = prec.prior) + 
  f(Year, model = "iid", hyper = prec.prior) + 
  f(Yr_id, model = "rw1", hyper = prec.prior) + 
  f(CNT_time_id, model = "iid", hyper = prec.prior)

model1 <- inla(formula1, family="gaussian", data=DF,
               control.predictor=list(compute=T), control.inla=list(h=0.168063), 
               control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, waic=TRUE), verbose=TRUE, keep=TRUE)


NB: Include another space index variable and specifying iid works without error. e.g 
formula1a <- U5MR ~ SEC + FEMP + GDP + OPH + HEXP + WATER + DEF + SANI + PM2.5 +
  f(OBJECTID, model = "bym2", graph = Global.adj.path, scale.model = TRUE, hyper = prec.prior) + 
   f(OBJECTID2, model = "iid",
  f(Year, model = "iid", hyper = prec.prior) + 
  f(Yr_id, model = "rw1", hyper = prec.prior) + 
  f(CNT_time_id, model = "iid", hyper = prec.prior)

I dropped the second area index variable because per my understand of https://www.paulamoraga.com/book-geospatial/sec-arealdatatheory.html  bym2 models both structured and unstructured spatial effects.

Regards,
